enbridge-mainline-lakehead.product: Crude oil, refined petroleum products and natural gas liquids
enbridge-mainline-lakehead.capacity_note: Multiple Mainline/Lakehead lines. CER lists nameplate capacity of 3,220,000 bbl/d exiting Gretna and 1,040,000 bbl/d into Sarnia; these are different system locations, not additive or ratings for every mapped segment.

enbridge-line-9.product: Light, medium and heavy crude oil
enbridge-line-9.capacity_note: CER reports 300,000 bbl/d operating capacity for Line 9. Available capacity depends on product mix and operating conditions.
enbridge-line-9.as_of: Current profile; use section updated August 2026

enbridge-bakken.origin: North Dakota gathering points / Berthold, North Dakota
enbridge-bakken.capacity_note: Includes the North Dakota gathering/interstate network and Canadian Line 26. Line 26 alone is rated about 145,000 bbl/d; this is not a capacity for all grouped lines.

enbridge-us-downstream.origin: Multiple Midwest / Midcontinent terminals; Cushing, Oklahoma, for Seaway
enbridge-us-downstream.destination: Regional refineries and Texas Gulf Coast connections
enbridge-us-downstream.capacity_note: Several distinct laterals and trunk systems share this map group. Seaway connects Cushing with the Houston region; capacities and endpoints differ by line.

trans-mountain-puget.product: Crude oil and refined petroleum products; Puget Sound carries crude oil
trans-mountain-puget.origin: Edmonton, Alberta; Sumas connection for Puget Sound
trans-mountain-puget.destination: Burnaby / Westridge, British Columbia; Anacortes / Ferndale, Washington
trans-mountain-puget.capacity_note: Expanded Trans Mountain nominal capacity is about 890,000 bbl/d. The separate Puget Sound branch is about 240,000 bbl/d with primarily light oil. These capacities are not additive.

keystone.destination: Illinois, Cushing and Texas Gulf Coast delivery points
keystone.capacity_note: 591,000 bbl/d is the Canadian Keystone mainline nameplate rating reported by CER. Downstream branches have separate constraints; this is not a guarantee of end-to-end available capacity.

express-platte.destination: Casper, Wyoming; onward on Platte to Wood River, Illinois
express-platte.capacity_note: Express is rated 310,000 bbl/d; Platte is rated 145,000–164,000 bbl/d depending on section. Connected systems have different capacities and cannot be summed into one route rating.

southern-lights.capacity_note: Annual-average capacity after the Line 13 expansion. The 2025 annual report lists 198,000 bbl/d, superseding older 180,000 bbl/d descriptions. This is capacity, not observed throughput.

cochin.capacity_note: Pembina reports annual-average capacity of 110,000 bbl/d for the condensate import route from Kankakee to Fort Saskatchewan. This is capacity, not observed throughput.
cochin.source_name: Pembina — 2025 Annual Information Form, PDF page 38

wascana.origin: Raymond / Montana–Saskatchewan border, via Bakken North
wascana.capacity_note: CER reports approximately 40,000 bbl/d pipeline capacity. This applies to Wascana, not the capacity of the interconnected Bakken North or Enbridge systems.

westspur.destination: Enbridge Mainline connection at Cromer, Manitoba
westspur.capacity_note: CER reports approximately 247,400 bbl/d system capacity. Individual gathering branches and delivery paths have different constraints.

milk-river.origin: Bow River interconnection near Milk River, Alberta
milk-river.destination: Front Range interconnection at the U.S. border west of Coutts
milk-river.capacity_note: CER reports approximately 97,900 bbl/d capacity for Milk River. It is operated by Milk River Pipeline Ltd., an Inter Pipeline subsidiary; downstream U.S. capacity is separate.

enbridge-lines-7-11.product: Light, medium and heavy crude oil
enbridge-lines-7-11.capacity_note: Operator annual-average capacities are 180,000 bbl/d for Line 7 and 117,000 bbl/d for Line 11. The connected lines are not additive.
enbridge-lines-7-11.source_name: Enbridge — Energy Infrastructure Assets, pages 20 and 23

trans-northern.destination: Ontario–Québec distribution network, including GTA and Ottawa
trans-northern.capacity_note: Segment capacities vary. CER lists 60,000–132,000 bbl/d across the eastern network's principal sections. The operator's 172,900 bbl/d average shipment figure is throughput, not capacity.

imperial-sarnia-products.destination: Greater Toronto / Hamilton; Finch terminal in North York
imperial-sarnia-products.capacity_note: No current full-system nameplate capacity was found in the reviewed primary sources. The Waterdown–Finch replacement is in service; the route shown is an approximate corridor.
imperial-sarnia-products.source_name: Imperial — Sarnia Products Pipeline / Waterdown to Finch

sun-canadian.destination: London, Hamilton and Toronto-area marketing terminals
sun-canadian.capacity_note: The operator publishes the served origins and destinations but no current nameplate capacity in its reviewed system description. No capacity is inferred from diameter or refinery output.

valero-pipeline-saint-laurent.capacity_note: Current operator information does not state installed capacity. Historical project ratings are not treated as a verified current nameplate rating.

vantage.origin: Bakken gas plants near Tioga, North Dakota
vantage.destination: AEGS connection near Empress, Alberta, via Saskatchewan
vantage.capacity_note: Pembina reports 68,000 bbl/d for the Vantage system including gathering laterals. The map also names Stateline II; no separate rating for that lateral was verified, and capacities are not summed.
vantage.source_name: Pembina — 2025 Annual Information Form, PDF page 38

norman-wells.capacity_note: Historical annual-average pipeline capacity. Imperial shut in source production in August 2026; this rating does not imply current throughput or available service. Pipeline deactivation status remains unverified.
norman-wells.as_of: Historical rating; source production shut in August 2026

other-cer-liquids.product: Genesis: petrochemical feedstocks; Montréal: crude oil
other-cer-liquids.origin: Genesis: Michigan / Corunna area; Montréal: Portland supply via Highwater border
other-cer-liquids.destination: Genesis: Sarnia-area petrochemical sites; Montréal: Montréal-Est
other-cer-liquids.capacity_note: Two unrelated systems are grouped: Genesis petrochemical feedstock lines and the Canadian portion of Portland–Montréal. They have different products, directions and capacities; no combined rating applies.
other-cer-liquids.source_name: CER — Genesis and Montréal pipeline profiles

us-crude-trunk-reference.origin: Multiple origins; not supplied as fields by EIA
us-crude-trunk-reference.destination: Multiple delivery points; not supplied as fields by EIA
us-crude-trunk-reference.capacity_note: National reference network, not one pipeline. EIA supplies names, operators and geometry but no capacity or endpoint fields. No flow direction or capacity is inferred from coordinate order.
us-crude-trunk-reference.source_name: EIA Energy Atlas — Crude-oil trunk pipelines

us-hgl-reference.origin: Multiple origins; not supplied as fields by EIA
us-hgl-reference.destination: Multiple delivery points; not supplied as fields by EIA
us-hgl-reference.capacity_note: National reference network, not one pipeline. EIA supplies names, operators and geometry but no capacity or endpoint fields. No flow direction or capacity is inferred from coordinate order.
us-hgl-reference.source_name: EIA Energy Atlas — Hydrocarbon gas liquids pipelines

rangeland-aurora-glacier.destination: Billings, Montana, via the Carway border connection
rangeland-aurora-glacier.capacity_note: Rangeland, Aurora and Glacier have different component capacities. CER reports about 45,000 bbl/d for the short Aurora border link; this is not a rating for the full grouped route.
rangeland-aurora-glacier.source_name: CER — Aurora; Phillips 66 — Glacier operating agreement

us-products-buckeye.destination: Midwest and Northeast U.S. distribution markets
us-products-buckeye.capacity_note: Buckeye reports delivered volumes and mileage for its wider portfolio, not a single nameplate capacity for these 31 EIA Buckeye-labelled source features. Laurel and other named Buckeye systems are separate selections.
us-products-buckeye.as_of: Operator review 2026-10-10; Underlying EIA inventory date unavailable; copy service data edit 2025-07-01

us-products-colonial.capacity_note: Brookfield's Q2 2025 letter reports 2.5 million bbl/d system capacity and confirms its acquisition. This dated system rating is not observed throughput, individual branch capacity, or a new survey of the EIA geometry.
us-products-colonial.source_name: Brookfield Infrastructure — Q2 2025 letter to unitholders
us-products-colonial.as_of: Brookfield Q2 2025 letter; Colonial acquisition completed July 31, 2025; Underlying EIA inventory date unavailable; copy service data edit July 1, 2025

us-products-magellan.destination: Multiple delivery markets; not individual endpoints in EIA attributes
us-products-magellan.capacity_note: ONEOK confirms its September 2023 Magellan acquisition. EIA retains MIDSTREAM PARTNERS as its operator attribute. No single current capacity has been verified for these 72 Magellan-labelled source records.
us-products-magellan.source_name: ONEOK — completion of Magellan acquisition, September 25, 2023
